Case No.102 dated 26-02-2002. Upon completion of the investigation, police submitted charge sheet No.6 dated 13-05-2002   under Sections 147/148/323/324 /326/380/ 302/ 447/448 and 417 of the Penal Code against the petitioner and 59 others. Thereafter, the case was sent to the Court of Sessions at Brahmanbaria and was registered as Sessions Trial Case No.I28 of 2002 and was subsequently transferred in the Court of Additional Sessions Judge, Court No.2, Brahmanbaria for trial. During pendency of the trial, the case was transferred to the Druta Bichar Tribunal, Chittagong for trial in pursuance to S. R.O. No.210 Ain/2004 and the said S. R. 0. was published in Bangladesh Official Gazette on 10th July, 2004 and the case being mentioned in serial No.78 of the said gazette was registered as Druta Bichar Case No.22 of 2004 of the Druata Bichar Tribunal, Chittagong. Over the selfsame occurrence, the petitioner as informant lodged a First Information Report with the Nabinagar Police Station which was numbered as G. R. Case No.102 of 2002; that after investigation the police also submitted charge sheet in the case being No.I13 dated 06-07-2002 against 39 persons as accuseds under Sections 143/447/323/324/354/379 and 380 of the Penal Code. Thereafter, the petitioner filed Criminal Motion No.33 of 2003 in the Court of the learned Sessions Judge, Brahmanbaria, under section 526 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for transfer of the case in the Court of Additional Sessions Judge, 2nd Court, Brahmanbaria to be tried simultaneously with Sessions Trial : Case No.128 of 2002 and the learned Sessions Judge, Brahmanbaria by his judgment and order dated 29-01-2004 allowed the Motion and transferred the said G. R. Case No.102 of 2002 from the Court of Magistrate, First Class, Nabinagar to the Court of Additional Sessions Judge, 2nd Court, Brahmanbaria for an analogous trial of both the cases. The petitioner, thereafter, filed an application on 21-11-2004 before the Druta Bichar Tribunal, Chittagong praying for an analogous hearing of the aforesaid G. R. Case No.102 of 2002 of the Court of Magistrate, First Class, Nabinagar, District of Brahmanbaria along with Druta Bichar Case No.22 of 2004 of the Court of Druta Bichar Tribunal, Chittagong on the ground that the said G. R. Case N0.102 of 2002 is, the counter case of Druta Bichar Case No.22 of 2004 and the petitioner would be seriously prejudiced if the trial of the two cases is not held simultaneously and that for proper adjudication both the case should be heard simultaneously. The, learned Druta Bichar Tribunal by its order dated 21-11-2004 rejected the said application for analogous hearing on the ground that the learned Tribunal lacked jurisdiction to try the G. R. Case No.IO2 of 2002 along with Druta Bichar Case No.22 of 2004.
